exposure: by state (Wisconsin, Florida, and New York)
cohort: All nonfederal hospital births in Wisconsin, Florida, and New York
finding: Clinical and nonclinical factors, particularly patient demographics, previous cesareans, hospital markup ratios, and social determinants of health, explained a substantial proportion of the variation in cesarean rates across states, while cesarean delivery was associated with higher healthcare utilization and costs.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with higher postpartum readmissions, unplanned emergency department visits, greater lengths of stay, and hospital costs across all states.
